prompt: What does `Genre.HISTORY.ordinal()` return for `enum Genre { FICTION, HISTORY, SCIENCE, POETRY }`?
hint: Positions are counted from 0.

choices.why: That would be counting from 1; `values()` printed `1 HISTORY`.
Right: its position in the declared order, starting at 0.

choices.text: The string `"HISTORY"`
choices.why: That is `name()`; `ordinal()` is a number.

choices.text: A number that changes on every run
choices.why: It is fixed by the source: the order the constants are written in.

prompt: Lesson 7 warned against `==` for strings. Why is `picked == Genre.HISTORY` correct for an enum?
hint: How many `HISTORY` objects exist in a running program?

choices.text: Because `==` on an enum compares the names letter by letter
choices.why: `==` compares references for every object; it works here for another reason.

choices.text: Because each constant is one object, made once
choices.why: Right: `valueOf` returned that same object, so identity and equality coincide.

choices.text: Because the compiler rewrites `==` into `equals` for enums
choices.why: The compiler rewrites nothing; there is just no second `HISTORY` to compare against.

prompt: `Genre.valueOf("history")` ended the program. With what?
hint: `valueOf` is exact about names.

choices.text: It returned `null`, and the next line threw `NullPointerException`
choices.why: It never returned; the exception came from inside `valueOf`.

choices.text: It returned `HISTORY`, because enum names ignore case
choices.why: Case matters: there is no constant called `history`.

choices.text: `IllegalArgumentException: No enum constant Genre.history`
choices.why: Right: a name the enum does not have is refused loudly.

prompt: `Floors` has a `switch` expression over `Genre` with no case for `POETRY`. What happens?
hint: A switch expression must produce a value for every input.

choices.text: It compiles, and `floor(POETRY)` returns `null`
choices.why: It never compiles; the compiler knows `POETRY` exists.

choices.text: It compiles, and throws at run time when `POETRY` arrives
choices.why: The error came from `javac`, before anything ran.

choices.text: `javac` refuses it, pointing at the incomplete switch
choices.why: Right: the compiler knows every constant and finds the missing one.

prompt: Every genre has a real answer in a `switch`. Why does the section advise leaving `default` out?
hint: Think about a genre added next year.

choices.text: So a constant added later fails to compile here
choices.why: Right: with `default`, the new genre falls into it and nothing points at this `switch`.

choices.text: Because `default` is not allowed in a switch over an enum
choices.why: It is allowed and compiles; the cost is the check it switches off.

choices.text: Because `default` makes the switch slower
choices.why: Speed is not the issue; what is lost is the compiler's help.

choices.text: Because `default` runs for every constant before its own case
choices.why: A `default` branch runs only when no case matches.

prompt: In `STANDARD(14, 50)`, what are `14` and `50`?
hint: Each constant's argument list is a call to something.

choices.text: Its ordinal and its hash code
choices.why: The ordinal comes from the position; these are values the constant carries.

choices.text: Constructor arguments, kept in fields
choices.why: Right: `days` becomes 14 and `centsPerDay` becomes 50 for that constant.

choices.text: Its minimum and its maximum
choices.why: Nothing in the enum checks a range; the constructor just stores them.

prompt: `SHORT` was built as `SHORT(3, 200)`. What does `LoanType.SHORT.feeCents(6)` return, in cents?
hint: Days late times cents per day.

prompt: `LoanType.REFERENCE.getClass()` printed `class LoanType$1`, while `SHORT.getClass()` printed `class LoanType`. Why?
hint: `REFERENCE` is the only constant with braces of its own.

choices.text: Because `REFERENCE` is the third constant
choices.why: Position does not create classes; `$1` numbers anonymous classes.

choices.text: Its body made it an object of an anonymous subclass
choices.why: Right: the compiler wrote `LoanType$1.class` for that body, and its `feeCents` overrides the default.

choices.text: Because its constructor arguments are both 0
choices.why: `REFERENCE(0, 0)` without a body would be a plain `LoanType`.

choices.text: Because enums put each constant in its own class file
choices.why: `STANDARD` and `SHORT` share `LoanType.class`; only the constant with a body got its own.

prompt: Why does `REFERENCE.feeCents` throw an exception instead of returning 0?
hint: What would a 0 mean to the code that adds fees up?

choices.text: Because an enum method may not return 0
choices.why: Any `long` may be returned; the choice is about meaning.

choices.text: Because `long` arithmetic overflows when `centsPerDay` is 0
choices.why: Multiplying by 0 gives 0 and overflows nothing.

choices.text: Because 0 would read as "no fee"
choices.why: Right: asking for the fee of a loan that cannot exist is a mistake, and the refusal makes it loud.

prompt: Which of these can an enum do? Choose all that apply.
hint: It already extends `java.lang.Enum`, and it is final.

choices.text: Have fields, a constructor and methods
choices.why: Yes: `LoanType` has all three.

choices.text: Implement an interface
choices.why: Yes: that is how an enum joins a design with other implementations, in lesson 23.

choices.text: Extend another class of yours
choices.why: It already extends `java.lang.Enum`, and a class has one superclass.

choices.text: Be extended by an ordinary class
choices.why: An enum is `final`, as `javap` showed.

prompt: `EnumSet.of(Genre.POETRY, Genre.FICTION)` printed `[FICTION, POETRY]`. Why that order?
hint: What order did `values()` print?

choices.text: Alphabetical order of the constants' names, A to Z
choices.why: It happens to match here; the rule is the declaration order, as `range` showed.

choices.text: The order the enum declares its constants
choices.why: Right: an `EnumSet` walks its bits in ordinal order.

choices.text: The reverse of the order they were added
choices.why: They were added `POETRY` first; the set ignores insertion order entirely.

prompt: `EnumSet.___(set)` returns every constant of the enum that is not in `set`.
hint: Section 04 printed `[HISTORY, SCIENCE]` with it.

prompt: Why does `new EnumMap<>(Genre.class)` take the enum's class as an argument?
hint: Underneath, it is an array indexed by ordinal.

choices.text: To know how long its internal array has to be
choices.why: Right: an array needs its length up front, and the class tells it.

choices.text: So that it can sort the keys alphabetically
choices.why: It keeps the declaration order, not the alphabet.

choices.text: Because generic type arguments are required at run time
choices.why: Lesson 35 shows they are erased; that is exactly why the class is passed explicitly.

choices.text: So that it can reject keys from other maps
choices.why: It rejects keys of other types, but that is not why the class is needed.

prompt: A program saved `SCIENCE` as its ordinal, 2. Somebody adds `BIOGRAPHY` at the top of the enum. What does the saved 2 read back as?
hint: Every constant after the insertion moves one place.

choices.text: As `SCIENCE`, because ordinals are fixed when a constant is first created
choices.why: Ordinals are positions in the current source, recomputed on every build.

choices.text: As an `IllegalArgumentException`, because 2 no longer matches
choices.why: Position 2 still exists, so nothing fails; that is the danger.

choices.text: As `HISTORY`, with no error at all
choices.why: Right: `Ordinals` printed `by ordinal: HISTORY`, a valid genre and the wrong one.

choices.text: As `BIOGRAPHY`, the new constant
choices.why: `BIOGRAPHY` is at 0; position 2 is now `HISTORY`.

prompt: What does the section recommend storing, for data that must outlive any edit to the enum, a rename included?
hint: Even `name()` breaks on a rename.

choices.text: The ordinal, with a comment saying that the list must never be reordered
choices.why: A comment is a habit; the first tidy-up breaks it, silently.

choices.text: `name()`, because names never change
choices.why: Names survive reordering but not renaming, which is why the section goes one step further.

choices.text: A code of your own, kept in a field of each constant
choices.why: Right: `SCIENCE("sci")` keeps its code through a reorder and a rename.

prompt: Put these in the order they happen for `enum Genre { ... }` in a program that prints `Genre.FICTION`.
hint: Lesson 27's order, and section 02's `javap`.
items: `javac` writes `Genre.class` with a field per constant
The program uses `Genre` for the first time
`Genre`'s class initialiser creates the four constants

prompt: Match each method to what it gives for `Genre.SCIENCE`.
hint: `SCIENCE` is the third constant.

prompt: A colleague replaces `Genre` with `static final int FICTION = 0, HISTORY = 1, ...` "to keep it simple". Which check from this lesson is lost?
hint: What did `Floors` get from the compiler?

choices.text: None: `int` constants are checked the same way
choices.why: The compiler cannot know which `int`s are genres, so it cannot check a `switch` or a parameter.

choices.text: A method taking a genre now accepts `7`, and a switch missing one compiles
choices.why: Right: both checks need the compiler to know every value there is.

choices.text: Only `valueOf`, which has no `int` equivalent
choices.why: That is the smaller loss; the type check on every use is the larger one.

prompt: A `LoanType` needs a new kind, `SUMMER`, lent for 30 days at 25 cents a day. What has to change?
hint: Where do `days()` and `feeCents` get their numbers?

choices.text: One line in the list of constants: `SUMMER(30, 25)`
choices.why: Right: the methods read fields, so the new constant answers them at once.

choices.text: The new line plus a case in each method
choices.why: Those methods have no `switch`; they read the constant's own fields.

choices.text: A new subclass of `LoanType`
choices.why: Nothing can extend an enum; a constant is enough.

choices.text: A constant-specific body overriding both methods
choices.why: Only behaviour that differs needs a body; these numbers fit the fields.

prompt: Where does an `EnumMap<Genre, Integer>` fit better than a `HashMap<Genre, Integer>`?
hint: The keys are the constants of one enum.

choices.text: Only when the map holds every constant of the enum
choices.why: It works with any subset; `counts` held three of four.

choices.text: Only when the program must store ordinals on disk
choices.why: An `EnumMap` uses ordinals in memory, which is safe; storing them is the mistake.

choices.text: Wherever the keys are an enum: it is smaller, faster and keeps the enum's order
choices.why: Right: that is why the section calls it the default choice.
